message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to very different mammalian lineages—lion is a member of the order **Carnivora** (family Felidae), while zebra is a member of the order **Perissodactyla** (family Equidae).  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the two orders, which lies deep within the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  

In other words, the common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae—a small placental mammal that lived roughly 50–70 million years ago during the late Paleocene–early Eocene, before the two lineages diverged into the distinct orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla.
